Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Lena Cho (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (Luna Tech - Dir ML), Tom Voss (Luna Tech - Platform), Rachel Li (Luna Tech - SRE), Ben Ortiz (Product)
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on results from the sprint on batching and caching. Redwood presented short benchmarks showing meaningful tokens-per-dollar improvements with tuned batching and prefix/KV cache. Customer raised concerns about tail latency and consistency for real-time user flows; agreed to run a 24h throughput test with production prompts and then reconvene. Security questions and pricing follow-ups assigned.
topics: next steps: 24h run, prompt set share, pricing, security Q&A
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): All right, hey everyone, thanks for making time. We're going to run through the sprint results on batching and caching, um, and then lock down next steps. Diego, do you want to kick off with the numbers?
[00:23] Diego (Redwood SE): Yeah, thanks. So quick recap: baseline run with default config we measured about ~420k tokens per dollar across the workload, with an average tokens/sec of ~1,200 and P95 latency around 420ms. After turning on continuous batching and bumping batch_target to 48 we saw tokens-per-dollar go up to ~580k (~38% improvement) and tokens/sec to ~1,650.
[01:10] Aisha (Luna Tech): Sorry, can you repeat the tokens-per-dollar numbers? I'm parsing that against our internal cost model.
[01:18] Diego: Sure — baseline 420k, tuned 580k. With prefix caching enabled on the most common prompts we got an extra ~18% saving on total generated tokens — so effectively pushing us towards ~680k tokens per dollar on repeat traffic.
[01:45] Tom (Luna Tech): When you say prefix caching, is that removing tokens from the response or skipping compute by reusing KV? I'm a little fuzzy.
[01:53] Lena (Redwood SE): Good question. There's two things: prefix cache reduces prompt tokens sent to the model by serving common prefixes from the cache (so fewer tokens billed/processed). KV cache reuses past attention key/value states so the model computes fewer FLOPs on repeated sequences. In our runs KV cache cut compute time on repeated context by about 30% on the subset we tested.
[02:30] Rachel (Luna Tech): That 30% — how did that translate into latency for interactive requests? Our concern is user-facing P95 not just average throughput.
[02:42] Diego: On cached paths P95 was great — dropped to ~160ms — but you see a mixed distribution: cold paths still hit 450+ ms P95. So overall P95 improved by ~12-15% depending on traffic mix. The tradeoff is batching — larger batch_target moves tokens/sec up but increases queuing latency for single-request flows.
[03:20] Ben (Luna Tech): For the chat UI we need sub-300ms P95 for short queries; is there a sweet spot that gets us better tokens-per-dollar without blowing past 300?
[03:32] Diego: From our experiments, batch_target around 32 to 48 with max_wait_ms tuned to 20 gave a decent compromise — tokens-per-dollar improved ~25% while keeping P95 ~320ms. If you push to batch_target 64 you'll see more throughput (additional ~12%) but P95 creeps above 350-380ms on cold requests.
[04:05] Aisha: Do you have the distribution data? I'd like the percent of requests that are cache hits vs cold.
[04:12] Diego: Yes — in our synthetic replay based on your sample traces, cache hit ratio was ~42% for prefix cache on core prompts. KV cache hit was lower, near 18% because of session variability. If Luna Tech can standardize certain system prompts we can push hit rates higher.
[04:48] Maya: Quick note on cost math — tokens-per-dollar here assumes current hosted pricing and the specific model variant we used (open-llama-13b-quant). Dedicated pricing numbers change unit economics; we'll provide a revised sheet.
[05:05] Tom: Also, how stable are these gains if we enable quantization or change model variants?
[05:12] Lena: Quantization (4-bit) improves compute efficiency but sometimes reduces quality slightly; for many prompts it's fine and it boosts tokens-per-dollar another ~10-15% in our bench. Switching to a smaller model variant with similar quality also helps. We'll include a table in the follow-up.
[05:38] Rachel: Security question — KV cache means storing intermediate layer states, is that encrypted at rest?
[05:45] Lena: Good callout. In Redwood Private and Dedicated we encrypt cache at rest and it can be routed through customer KMS. For hosted we also encrypt but you may want to push to a dedicated pool with your KMS for sensitive data. We'll add that to the security Q&A.
[06:10] Aisha: On throughput tests — can you do a 24 hour replay with our real prompt set? Our peak diurnal patterns matter.
[06:18] Maya: Yes — Diego will run a continuous 24h run with batch_target=64 and an alternate run with batch_target=32 and we will share full CSVs for tokens/sec, cost, P50/P95/P99.
[06:36] Diego: Quick caveat — the 24h run will surface autoscaling behavior and burst capacity usage which affects hourly costs. We'll annotate the logs with instance types and GPU utilization.
[06:50] Ben: Can you also include records of KV hit ratios over time? We want to see if cold-starts near midnight drop hit ratio.
[06:58] Diego: Yep we'll include hit ratios and TTL decay behavior.
[07:05] Tom: About batching settings — you mentioned max_wait_ms. If we lower max_wait_ms to 10ms it improves tail latency but reduces batching efficiency, right?
[07:14] Diego: Exactly. Lowering max_wait_ms from 20 to 10 shaves queuing by ~40ms but drops throughput gains by ~8-10%. It's a knobs tradeoff.
[07:32] Aisha: One more question on billing: tokens-per-dollar in these slides — do they include infrastructure overhead like network egress and storage?
[07:40] Maya: The numbers in the quick bench are compute-centric. We'll provide a full cost model including egress, storage, and dedicated reserved capacity amortization in the pricing follow-up.
[07:55] Rachel: For our SREs, P99 matters — did you see any pathological tails with batching?
[08:04] Diego: There were a handful of outliers tied to autoscaler scaling events; P99 spiked to >1s during scale-up. We recommend warm pool strategies (idle instances) for strict P99 SLOs; dedicated pools help there.
[08:25] Ben: If we move to a dedicated pool what's the interplay with fallback? Do we still get graceful fallback to hosted model variants?
[08:33] Lena: Yes — routing policies can fall back across tiers and to smaller variants if capacity constrained. You can pin critical routes to dedicated with a fallback chain.
[08:45] Aisha: Operationally, what changes will we need on our side to get better cache hit ratios? Some prompts include user-specific IDs which break cache.
[08:55] Diego: Two suggestions: normalize system prompts to remove user IDs, or move user-specific data into a structured slot that isn't part of the cached prefix. Also increase TTL on prefixes that are stable.
[09:10] Tom: Will that affect compliance? We have to avoid persisting PII in caches.
[09:15] Lena: Right — caches can be configured to exclude PII or to store encrypted blobs under customer KMS and with stricter retention. We'll document configurations that meet common compliance needs.
[09:30] Maya: Alright let's talk immediate next steps — Diego will run the 24h. When we come back we'll compare batch_target 32 vs 64, look at tokens-per-dollar, P95, P99, KV hit ratios, and autoscaler events.
[09:46] Aisha: Sounds good. One ask — can Redwood mark the runs with the exact model binary / kernel versions so our infra team can reproduce?
[09:54] Diego: Yes — we'll export exact runtime versions, kernel flags, and quantization parameters.
[10:02] Ben: Anything else on pricing?
[10:05] Maya: I'll prepare a hosted vs dedicated pricing sheet that includes the tuned batch numbers and estimated monthly costs at your projected usage.
[10:12] Rachel: And security Q&A? Can we schedule a half hour next week?
[10:15] Lena: Yes, we'll coordinate. I'll bring audit log retention details and KMS notes.
[10:22] Tom: Quick tangent — competitors. Are there any model variants from Anthropic that would materially change this calculus?
[10:30] Diego: Some competitor models have different context caching behavior and latency profiles; we'll add a short comparison note but it's not a blocker to the bench.
[10:40] Aisha: Ok good. Thanks everyone.
[10:44] Maya: Wrap up — recap action items and owners. Diego 24h runs, Maya pricing, Aisha prompt sets, Rachel security questions. We'll meet next Thursday 15:00 to review.
[11:00] (crosstalk) Tom: Thanks, bye.
[11:05] End of recording.
